question: Where full_pass_pending is cleared, and what a fall-back does to the next hour.

struct_fields.name: full_pass_pending
struct_fields.comment: **Asks for the tick's full pass**: slot 73's full-pass flag is `hour == (id+6)%24 or this`. Seeded 1 (the constructor's `+0x84 = 0x10101`); set by CAIUnit::SetArea (0x4BBA17) and by 0x4D7F80 (0x4D8505); cleared by 0x4CC450 (0x4CC646), the first body of the tick's land block, which the full pass always reaches. So an agent's first hour with a unit, and the hour after any SetArea with one, is a full pass. **Read live** (FINDINGS-liveread.md, section 134): the Soviet Union's Smolensk HQ at 17 July 1941 enters the naval body at 15:00 unforced with this set, at 16:00 forced with it still set, at 17:00 forced with it clear - the fall-back sets it after 0x4CC450 has cleared it, so a defender pulled out on a full pass makes the next hour's pass full. Not cleared on 0x4CC450's early return (an agent with no root unit, or a non-root one with an area).
struct_fields.evidence: The sweep of 0x8AF000-0x8E0000 for byte stores to [reg+0x84] gives three: 0x4BBA17 and 0x4D8505 (1) and 0x4CC646 (bl, zero from 0x4CC473), on 0x4CC450's way to its end. The running game, CAIUnit_ManageNavalUnits' entry watched for the Soviet agents 17 July 12:00-18:00. Wrong if a forced naval pass ever follows an hour whose land block left the flag clear.
struct_fields.revises: comment - the live reading and what a fall-back on a full pass does to the next hour
